correctness.rationale: For any n>=1, the diagonal pair (k,k) truncates upper/lower pairs and forces independent prefix intervals. Conversely, the four product-type cases (upper/upper, lower/lower, mixed, diagonal) prove closure for arbitrary admissible reach vectors; mixed pairs (i,j) and (k,l) with i<j,l<k either reproduce (k,l) when k<i or lie in the upper prefix of (i,j) or lower prefix of (k,l) when i<=k. Inclusion is coordinatewise; the rank statistic counts exactly the sums of reach vectors; congruence classes are precisely convex intervals, so choices of n-1 cuts count them. Exhaustive all-reflexive-relation tests n=1..4, and independent code-generation tests n=2..5, returned VERIFY_OK. Finite checks do not prove the infinite n theorem; the symbolic argument does.

value.rationale: The 2026 motivating paper explicitly asks for semilattice DSC values, and its Clifford-semigroup theorem is parameterized by them. Finite meet-chains are a canonical infinite semilattice family; the explicit inclusion-lattice decomposition and squared inversion-number polynomial classify all reflexive compatible relations, not just a few coefficients. The exact rapidly vanishing ratio gives a natural meaningful special-family answer, with the limitation that branching semilattices remain open.
